claims: Mass is a fundamental physical quantity.
Mass represents the amount of matter in an object.
Mass represents an object's resistance to acceleration (inertia).
Mass is measured in kilograms (kg).
Mass is measured via balances or force-based scales.
Mass remains constant regardless of location or gravity, unlike weight.
Inertial mass is resistance to velocity change.
Gravitational mass is strength of gravitational attraction.
M = F/a.
Mass = density × volume.
Mass = weight / gravitational acceleration.
The SI base unit of mass is the kilogram (kg).
Common units of mass include grams (g), milligrams (mg), and pounds (lb).
Pounds are often used for weight.
Pounds can represent mass in certain systems.
Balance scales measure mass by comparing against known masses.
Spring scales measure gravitational force which is then used to infer mass.
Inertial mass measures an object's resistance to acceleration when a force is applied.
Gravitational mass determines the strength of the gravitational force exerted by or on the body.
Inertial mass and gravitational mass are considered equal.
The equality of inertial mass and gravitational mass is a concept key to the theory of relativity.
